title: The Ghost Ship's Creepiest Detail Was Fiction

lines.text: Found sailing the Atlantic. Nobody on board.
You know the legend: warm tea, breakfast on the table.
Most of that is fiction. Even the name.
December 1872, east of the Azores. Another crew spots a ship drifting.
The Mary Celeste. Her lifeboat: gone.
Six months of food and water still aboard.
Seventeen hundred barrels of alcohol in the hold.
A sounding rod lay on deck, as if someone had checked for leaks.
Three and a half feet of water below. Yet she was seaworthy.
So where did the warm tea come from?
In 1884, an anonymous magazine story renamed her Marie Celeste.
Many readers took it as fact. The author: Arthur Conan Doyle, before Sherlock Holmes.
The cosy breakfast scenes came from retellings like these. Not from the ship.
The leading theories are ordinary.
Alcohol fumes, and fear of an explosion.
Or a broken pump, and fear she was sinking.
Either way, they may have taken the lifeboat, and lost the ship.
Captain Briggs, his wife Sarah, two-year-old Sophia and seven crew were never found.
Would you have left? Tell me below.
After the last log entry, nine days passed. Until she was...

shots.description: Ship (build once, reuse; all primitives): two-masted brigantine ~31 m. Hull = box 31x7.5x4 m tapered at bow via bmesh (bow vertices scaled to 0.15 width, raised sheer 0.6 m), dark tarred-wood material, white waterline stripe; deck = plane with plank texture; low deckhouse box 6x4x1.6 m aft of mainmast; foremast = cylinder 0.35 m dia x 26 m with three square-sail yards (cylinders) and square sails (subdivided planes, slight cloth bulge via shape key, two of them furled = thin rolled cylinders); mainmast = cylinder x 27 m with a fore-and-aft gaff sail (quad plane between boom and gaff cylinders); bowsprit cylinder; rigging = curve lines; stern davits = two curved bent cylinders with EMPTY falls hanging (thin rope curves). Frame 1 already moving: the brigantine glides out of a fog bank toward camera at a slight angle, sails half-set and slack, deck empty, the wheel (torus + spokes at the stern) turning slightly on its own. Sea surface swelling.
shots.camera: low near-water angle, 35mm, slow push toward the bow, handheld amp 0.02 (boat-bob)
shots.lighting: overcast grey-green daylight (sun 0.6 soft, colour 0.75/0.85/0.8), thick fog

shots.description: LEGEND VERSION (stylised, desaturated sepia grade + film-grain): a cosy cabin (studio_lib room 4x3 m, wood panels) with a table set for breakfast: plates (flat cylinders), cups with rising steam wisps, a teapot (sphere + spout cylinder). Clearly marked as the legend.
shots.camera: slow dolly across the table 50mm, steam in foreground
fx: steam wisps from cups (particle smoke, small)

shots.description: Same cabin: the steam freezes, the image desaturates to grey and a red diagonal stamp hits: FICTION. A brass name board on the wall reading 'MARIE CELESTE' flickers.
shots.lighting: lamp flickers out to cold grey

shots.description: Map card: stylised North Atlantic: Portugal/Spain coast outline right, Azores dots left. A dotted line marks the brigantine's position east of the Azores; a second ship icon (the Dei Gratia) approaches from the west. Date stamp types on.
shots.camera: 2D overlay over dark sea plate, slow zoom

overlay.text:
EAST OF THE AZORES
North Atlantic

4 DECEMBER 1872
SPOTTED BY THE DEI GRATIA

shots.description: Stern of the brigantine: name board on the transom reads MARY CELESTE (text3d, painted white). Camera rises to the davits: two empty curved davit arms with cut rope ends swinging. No lifeboat.
shots.camera: crane up 35mm from transom name to empty davits
shots.lighting: overcast grey-green daylight (sun 0.6 soft, colour 0.75/0.85/0.8), thick fog

shots.description: Small storeroom below deck: shelves (luggage_shelf builder) stacked with sacks, small casks and water barrels; a flashlight/lantern sweeps across them.
shots.lighting: lantern warm spot from camera, darkness

shots.description: Cargo hold: rows of barrels (cylinders with mid bulge via simple deform, dark oak with iron hoops = thin torus rings) stacked in tiers into darkness, stencilled 'ALCOHOL' on a few. Water glints on the floor between rows.
shots.camera: slow dolly down the aisle between barrel stacks, 24mm
shots.lighting: shafts of grey light from an open hatch + lantern
fx: water surface on floor (reflective plane, low ripple)

shots.description: Close-up on the empty deck: an iron sounding rod (thin cylinder 1.2 m with notch marks, on a coiled line) lies on the planks next to an open pump-well cover. Camera tilts down to it.
shots.lighting: overcast grey-green daylight (sun 0.6 soft, colour 0.75/0.85/0.8), thick fog

shots.description: Cutaway diagram: the brigantine hull in side section (lib_murder.section_diagram style: flat-shaded, cyan line on black), a water level rises to a marked line at 3.5 ft in the hold, while the outer waterline stays normal. Then hull glows green: FLOATING.
MID-POINT TURN. Flash cut back to the sepia legend cabin, push straight into a steaming cup.

Document reveal: a Victorian magazine page slides in (paper style), title block and dense columns of illegible placeholder text; a highlighted line shows the name 'MARIE CELESTE'. No real page facsimile reproduced; recreated generically.

Victorian writing desk (lib_murder.desk + desk_lamp + book props): a pen rests on a manuscript; a faceless silhouette (char_figure, seated, back to camera) at the desk. A deerstalker hat (simple cap + flaps from primitives) sits on a side table, catching the light at the end of the shot.
shots.camera: slow arc 40mm around the desk, ends on the hat
characters: writer silhouette (char_figure seated, back to camera, no face)

shots.description: The sepia legend cabin (from S02) dissolves away piece by piece (objects scale to zero), revealing a neutral, empty grey cabin (no food, no props asserted as found; deliberately non-specific). Overlay: two columns LEGEND vs RECORD.
shots.lighting: sepia -> cold grey daylight from a skylight

overlay.text:
Warm tea, half-eaten meals:
added in later retellings

shots.description: Opens on a THEORIES title over the barrel hold (L14), then: a translucent, faint wavering haze (volume with low density, slight green tint) drifts between barrels; a hatch overhead slams open (rotation key) with a burst of pale light. Theory visualisation only.
shots.camera: low 24mm looking up toward the hatch
shots.lighting: dim + flash of pale light through hatch at 2.9 s

shots.description: Deck pump (two cylinders + lever) partly dismantled: parts lying beside it on the deck; water sloshing in the pump well. Theory visualisation only.
shots.lighting: overcast grey-green daylight (sun 0.6 soft, colour 0.75/0.85/0.8), thick fog

shots.description: DRAMATISATION: a small open lifeboat (half-ellipsoid hull, 6 m) with dim, faceless silhouettes floats in fog while the brigantine, sails filled, slowly pulls away and vanishes into the fog. No harm shown.
shots.camera: from lifeboat level, 35mm, locked; ship recedes
characters: 8-10 tiny seated silhouettes in lifeboat (char_figure, no faces, low detail)
shots.lighting: overcast grey-green daylight (sun 0.6 soft, colour 0.75/0.85/0.8), thick fog, fog thickening

shots.description: Respect card: calm grey sea at dusk, a single lantern (point light inside glass cylinder) floats/bobs on a small plank. Memorial overlay with the names.

overlay.text:

shots.description: The empty deck at the wheel, seen from behind: wheel turning by itself a few degrees, fog rolling across.
shots.lighting: overcast grey-green daylight (sun 0.6 soft, colour 0.75/0.85/0.8), thick fog
